_note: 3BEQ grid, 21 rows, normal signal set (run `make signals-normal` first). THE INPUT CONTROL IS LIN FOR EVERY ROW -- there is no MAX row here; the input stage is already measured (docs/input-stage-2026-09-16.md) and a hot input would fold its hard clip into the EQ fit. Block 1 only: COMP off, WAH off, DST off, and every Block 2 slot off. Output Level stays at the campaign's fixed ~55% mark. Row 1 is the flat reference (all bands 0, Trim 0) that every other row is divided by in analysis/eq_response.py; capture it FIRST, and if the session runs long capture it again at the end so drift is visible. The captures/AX30G_BYPASS_IN-LIN.wav bypass capture is the fallback reference if row 1 is missing.
_note_mid_freq: Mid Freq steps (Mark, read off the unit 2026-09-17): 250, 315, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1k, 1.25k, 1.6k, 2k, 2.5k, 3.15k, 4k Hz -- 13 ISO third-octave steps. The rows below use 250 / 1000 / 4000, all real steps. The unit displays Trim as "Trim Gain"; the param key here stays "Trim" for the analysis.
_note_segments: Which segments carry the answer: sweep = the magnitude/phase curve (primary, Farina/cross-spectrum against the reference channel); noise = independent cross-check of the same curve; clicks = impulse response, third check and the phase sanity check; sine20/sine40 = a two-level check that the EQ is linear (a band at +16 dB should move both by the same dB); ramp = the only place EQ-stage clipping can show (see the last row); di = listening.

_note: Trim law, three points. Trim should be a flat broadband gain; if these three rows are not flat versus row 1, Trim is not a plain gain.

PRE- OR POST-EQ: Trim -18 with Bass +16. If Trim is a gain anywhere in the block the measured curve is (Bass +16 curve) - 18 dB exactly, because a linear EQ and a scalar commute. What this row actually decides is whether the EQ stage OVERFLOWS: with Trim pre-EQ the +16 dB bass boost happens on an already -18 dB signal and stays clean, whereas post-EQ the boost happens first and may clip inside the DSP. So compare this row's shape (after removing 18 dB) with the Bass +16 row's shape: a shape difference at the low end, or harmonics of 1 kHz on the sine/ramp segments in only one of the two, places Trim.
Bass band, four points: corner frequency, shelf-vs-peak shape, and whether cut mirrors boost.
Mid band at the LOWEST Mid Freq step. +-16 gives the center frequency and Q at full boost and full cut; a constant-Q design and a proportional-Q design differ most between these two.
Mid band at the MIDDLE Mid Freq step (see _note_mid_freq on row 1 -- capture whatever the unit's real middle step is and let the file name record it).
Mid band at the HIGHEST Mid Freq step.
Q VERSUS GAIN: half gain at the middle step. Constant Q -> this curve is the +16 curve scaled by 1/2 in dB at every frequency; proportional Q -> it is wider in relative bandwidth than half.

DOES THE EQ CLIP: everything boosted to maximum with Trim at its maximum too. Read the ramp and sine20 segments for harmonics of 1 kHz that the flat reference does not have, and the sweep for a response that is level-dependent (compare the sweep-derived curve with the noise-derived curve -- they diverge if the stage is clipping, because the two segments have different crest factors). Combined with the Trim -18 / Bass +16 row this says where the headroom limit sits in the block.
